newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish Treasury sets volumes for bond auctions.
newsitem.headline: Spanish Treasury sets volumes for bond auctions.

text.p: Spanish Treasury and the Bank of Spain announced the following expected volumes and maximum amounts (in billions of pesetas) to be placed at this week's auctions on July 1 and 2.

For the first time ever, the Spanish Treasury is offering bonds which will be strippable after the volume outstanding reaches at least one trillion pesetas and the Treasury authorises an issue as strippable.
ISSUE Expected amount Maximum amount Auction date
New bonds are all new references, with lower coupons. They are exempt from the payment of 25 percent witholding tax for legal entities.

The three-year bond, maturing on January 31, 2001, has a five percent coupon, the five-year, maturing on Juanuary 31 2003, has a 5.25 percent coupon. The 10-year, maturing on January 31, 2008, has a 6.00 percent coupon. And the 15-year bond, maturing on Juanuary 31, 2013, has a 6.15 percent coupon.
